doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Who decides what horns stay; producers asking for another take
summary: The producer has the last say; brass players do not improve with endless takes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Who makes the call in a situation, a typical pop situation, that your horn parts are on the record or they end up on the cutting room floor?

Always — well not always — but the producer is always has the last say. Sometimes, depending on how big the artist is, the artist can have a say in it, but you know it’s generally the producer. Because I mean a lot of times the artist isn’t even there when we do the horn parts.
Have you ever had a producer who was inclined to say, “Guys that was perfect, let’s do another one”?
Oh all the time you know, yeah.

Well just — you know they’re trying to get the magic somehow and they don’t kind of always realize that, especially with brass instruments (trumpets included) it’s not necessarily the more times you play it the better it’s going to get. You know there’s a point at which it starts going downhill kind of in a hurry, especially when it’s really intense and involved and technically difficult. So fortunately I’ve had enough success
that I can say that’s, you know, “It’s never going to get any better than that.” You know. “If you don’t like the way that sounds I can change it but you know that was really good.” So you know —
